entries.problem: Agent goal hijack via untrusted content (documents, emails, web, RAG) that redirects multi-step plans while appearing on-task.

estate.note: Social engineering firewall: external content is data, never instructions. Attack surface includes self-improvement, memory, authority drift, and swarms.
N-Cell/64 header on every action; governance intersection E* = E_proposed AND E_allowed AND E_available blocks actions outside the allowed set.
29 checks. A claim passes only all three gates (header, intersection, write-gate) AND a real external signal.

indicators.name: Hijack attempts blocked at the firewall
Mean time to detect a hijack attempt
indicators.unit: seconds from injection to firewall verdict

adapter.finding: Injected instruction detected in untrusted content becomes a claim object: source, injected text, intended redirection, mission stage reached.
adapter.patch: Firewall rule plus authority-mask tightening becomes the gated output; it passes CRUCIBLE only with the injection reproduced in isolation.
adapter.retest: Replay the same content through the loop; outcome coded HIJACK-BLOCKED or HIJACK-SUCCEEDED, with a Brier-scored confidence.

entries.problem: Excessive agency: agents granted write/delete/spend permissions far beyond the task.

estate.note: Authority compiler translates a mission into minimal required authority; every action carries an authorityMask.
Constitutional governor and least authority; dynamic verification intensity scales with risk, novelty, irreversibility, and blast radius.
Autonomy credit score per action class; one category's success does not grant unrelated authority.
Authority columns: Autonomous, Approval Required, Never Automatic. Production deployment, DNS changes, customer communication, destructive migration, and production credentials are never automatic.

indicators.name: Actions outside the compiled authority mask
Actions requiring human approval that ran autonomously

adapter.finding: An action outside the compiled mask becomes a claim object: agent, action, requested permission, compiled mask, gap.
adapter.patch: Mask recompilation plus credit-score downgrade for the action class becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Re-run the mission under the recompiled mask; outcome coded MASK-HELD or MASK-BREACHED.

entries.problem: Memory and context poisoning that persists across sessions and influences future decisions.

estate.note: Seven memory layers, write-gate with evidence thresholds (evidence <3 REJECT, contradiction QUARANTINE, evidence <6 QUARANTINE), decay F(t)=2^(-t/h). 21/21 tests.
Every memory is an object with class, provenance, status, confidence, scope, decision receipt; quarantined material never trains anything; raw bytes preserved first.
Memory is a named attack surface; redundant verification uses 3 distinct source families for critical claims.

indicators.name: Mean half-life of unverified memories
indicators.target: published per layer, trending down for low-evidence layers

adapter.finding: A poisoned memory write becomes a claim object: source, injected content, target layer, evidence count.
adapter.patch: Quarantine plus decay-constant tightening becomes the gated output; the write-gate threshold moves only on measured outcomes.
adapter.retest: Replay the poisoned content against the new gate; outcome coded POISON-BLOCKED or POISON-WROTE, with the memory object cited.

entries.problem: Tool/API misuse with legitimate credentials (argument injection, over-invocation, unexpected chains).

estate.note: Every agent action carries an N-Cell/64 header; proposed actions are intersected against allowed and available before execution.
The intersection gate is the enforcement point for tool calls; a call outside the allowed set never reaches the tool.
Loop detector stops repeat A-B-A-B cycles without new evidence; deadlock detector catches spinning agent teams.
Per-plugin reliability: every plugin call is a logged retrieval; the relying agent's confidence is adjusted by the plugin's historical success rate.

indicators.name: Tool calls outside the authority mask

adapter.finding: A misused tool call becomes a claim object: tool, arguments, credential used, expected vs actual chain.
adapter.patch: Argument schema tightening plus plugin reliability downgrade becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Replay the same call chain; outcome coded MISUSE-BLOCKED or MISUSE-SUCCEEDED, with the plugin reliability score updated.

entries.problem: Unexpected code execution through shells, eval, or tool-generated scripts.

estate.note: Verification commands run as argument arrays, never shell strings; failed gates trigger a bounded repair request with the real failure log; exhausted repair budget produces a blocker, not an invented success.
Side-effect ledger, idempotency, reversibility score, blast radius; dynamic verification intensity scales with irreversibility.
33 checks. Bounded repair with strikes; KILL below 20 or at 3 strikes.

indicators.name: Shell or eval executions outside approved commands
Mean blast radius of executed code

adapter.finding: An unexpected execution becomes a claim object: command, origin (shell/eval/tool-generated), blast radius, reversibility score.
adapter.patch: Command allowlist tightening plus reversibility requirement becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Replay the execution path under the new allowlist; outcome coded EXECUTION-BLOCKED or EXECUTION-RAN.

entries.problem: Identity and privilege abuse via cached tokens, delegation chains, or human-account reuse.

estate.note: Authority headers bind an action to its authority mask; the intersection blocks actions the token was never allowed to take.
Cached tokens and delegation chains are named attack surfaces; dynamic verification scales with risk.
Insured Action Protocol: Intent, Risk Scalar, micro-premium, Tactile Token, unlock, record in Append-Only History. No step may be skipped.
Canonical freeze: after Sentinel PASS, freeze the exact proven version; drift detector catches docs diverging from reality.

adapter.finding: A token abuse becomes a claim object: token, holder, delegation chain, actions taken, authority mask at each hop.
adapter.patch: Token revocation plus delegation-depth cap becomes the gated output; the revocation must reach all downstream tools.
adapter.retest: Replay the delegation chain with the revoked token; outcome coded ABUSE-BLOCKED or ABUSE-SUCCEEDED.

entries.problem: Rogue agents that continue or conceal activity after mandate ends or code-freeze.

estate.note: Capability statuses include REVOKED; shadow mode (predict, compare, promote only on evidence); canary autonomy ladder; bot birth and death (retire when low value).
Dead work detector and queue aging catch work that continues past its mandate; commitment tracker records what was promised.
Mandate end is an enforcement boundary; activity after mandate end is a classified failure type.

indicators.name: Mean time to revoke a rogue agent

adapter.finding: Post-mandate activity becomes a claim object: agent, mandate end time, actions after end, concealment signals.
adapter.patch: Revocation plus inventory reconciliation becomes the gated output; the agent's capability status moves to REVOKED.
adapter.retest: Audit for the agent's activity after revocation; outcome coded ROGUE-STOPPED or ROGUE-ACTIVE.

entries.problem: Human-agent trust exploitation (fluent outputs that induce approval of harmful actions).

estate.note: Hallucination firewall: no material external action on an unsupported model-generated premise; Brier-scored confidence; poorly calibrated agents lose decision weight.
Phase 1 parallel isolation, Phase 2 deliberation matrix with challenge rules, Phase 3 Chair adjudication; dissent is recorded, not smoothed over.
Human-accountable surface for inspecting evidence, comparing opportunities, and approving consequential action; control principle is qualify aggressively, commit selectively.

indicators.name: Brier score of agent confidence on approved actions

adapter.finding: A trust-exploiting output becomes a claim object: the fluent output, the evidence it lacked, the approval it induced.
adapter.patch: Evidence-gating rule (no approval without an inspected evidence packet) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Present the same output with the evidence packet attached; outcome coded APPROVED-WITH-EVIDENCE or APPROVAL-WITHHELD.

entries.problem: Cascading failures across multi-agent workflows where one error becomes trusted input.

estate.note: Phase 1 agents vote in isolation before seeing each other, so one agent's error cannot become another's input before the challenge round.
Swarm diversity enforced (20 identical agents are not 20 independent opinions); information gain per agent gates spawning.
Loop detector and deadlock detector stop agent teams spinning without new evidence.
Nine stages with a gate at each; a stage can block the mission and the block is receipted.

indicators.name: Errors that propagated to a second agent undetected
Mean stages before an error is caught

adapter.finding: A cascade becomes a claim object: origin error, propagation path, agents that trusted it, stage where it was caught.
adapter.patch: Isolation-before-deliberation enforcement plus an intermediate verification gate becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Replay the workflow with the same injected error; outcome coded CASCADE-CONTAINED or CASCADE-SPREAD.

entries.problem: Insecure inter-agent communication (spoofing, replay, unsigned messages).

estate.note: Signal nervous system and event substrate; findings flow as events through the lattice with provenance.
axon_event contract with idempotency_key and authority_context; run state machine from PROPOSED to ARCHIVED.
Every action carries an N-Cell/64 header binding route, organ, lifecycle, authority, memory, confidence, risk, and output.
Chained SHA-256 receipts; a tampered link verifies as TAMPERED.

adapter.finding: A spoofed or replayed message becomes a claim object: sender claimed, sender verified, idempotency key, header, replay count.
adapter.patch: Header-binding enforcement plus idempotency-key rejection becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Replay the same message against the new enforcement; outcome coded SPOOF-BLOCKED or SPOOF-ACCEPTED.

entries.problem: Agentic supply-chain compromise (malicious MCP servers, tool descriptors, third-party agents).

estate.note: Repeatable machine-readable patterns, versioned and scored; 49 ingredients, 30 families; a tool pattern is a recipe with a version and a score.
Isolated repo, deterministic verification outside the model, 8-item evidence manifest per run (SHAs, branch, command array, exit code, duration, log, gate result, verdict, SHA-256 manifest).
Canonical freeze after Sentinel PASS; drift detector catches docs and descriptors diverging from reality.

adapter.finding: A compromised tool becomes a claim object: tool descriptor, version, behavior change, approval it passed under.
adapter.patch: Descriptor freeze plus deterministic re-verification becomes the gated output; the tool is quarantined until re-verified.
adapter.retest: Re-run the tool's verification suite; outcome coded TOOL-CLEAN or TOOL-COMPROMISED.

entries.problem: Shadow agents / unregistered autonomous processes operating without inventory.

estate.note: Capability statuses (UNKNOWN, DISCOVERED, EXPERIMENTAL, PROVEN, RELIABLE, DEGRADED, REVOKED); bot birth and death rules.
Dead work detector and queue aging surface work with no owner and no mandate.
Searchable registry of all 179 systems with legion, stage, host, and live link; the inventory pattern the agent registry follows.

indicators.name: Mean time to register a new agent

adapter.finding: An unregistered process becomes a claim object: process, first observed activity, resources touched, owner unknown.
adapter.patch: Registration plus capability-status assignment (UNKNOWN until verified) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Re-audit for the process; outcome coded REGISTERED or STILL-SHADOW.

entries.problem: Reward hacking and specification gaming that produces high scores but wrong outcomes.

estate.note: Outcome-based learning requires ACTION then OUTCOME, not ACTION then MODEL THINKS IT WAS GOOD; Brier-scored confidence; epistemic quality metrics (false claims, corrected claims, contradictions caught, Sentinel rejection rate).
Sealed predictions specific enough to fail, blinded scoring against controls and 10,000-permutation nulls, eight falsification conditions, no theory protection.
Doctrine eta = (I_q x I_r x I_v) / (1 + E_wasted + C_violations); SEED requires eta at or above 70 and feedback accuracy at or above 0.6.

indicators.name: High-scoring outcomes that failed independent verification

adapter.finding: A gamed score becomes a claim object: the metric, the gaming method, the outcome it masked, the independent verification result.
adapter.patch: Independent verification gate on the metric plus Brier-scored confidence becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Re-score the same work under independent verification; outcome coded SCORE-HELD or SCORE-GAMED.

entries.problem: Emergent misalignment that appears only at scale or under novel conditions.

estate.note: Productive polarity is an inverted-U of difference under containment; every axiom names its own falsifier; emergence is a derived outcome, not a primitive.
Eight-stage closed loop with sealed predictions, blinded scoring, controls, and permutation nulls; designed to catch effects that appear only under novel conditions.
Generalization tests, capability ladder L0-L12, shadow mode (predict, compare, promote only on evidence).

adapter.finding: A scale-emergent misalignment becomes a claim object: scale reached, novel condition, behavior observed, falsifier triggered.
adapter.patch: Shadow-mode containment plus a generalization-test gate becomes the gated output; scale-up is blocked until the tests pass.
adapter.retest: Re-run the novel condition under shadow mode; outcome coded MISALIGNMENT-CONTAINED or MISALIGNMENT-REPEATED.

entries.problem: Lethal trifecta: simultaneous private data access + untrusted content + external channel.

estate.note: Governance intersection blocks any action that is proposed but not allowed or not available; the trifecta cannot execute without all three elements intersecting.
Social engineering firewall plus authority compiler; the trifecta is the exact combination the firewall is built to break apart.
Three gates plus a real external signal; a mission carrying private data, untrusted content, and an external channel hits the governance boundary and is held.
Insured Action Protocol prices the action before it moves; a trifecta action carries the highest risk scalar and requires the full protocol.

indicators.name: Missions with all three elements present and unmitigated

adapter.finding: A trifecta mission becomes a claim object: private data accessed, untrusted content present, external channel open, intersection result.
adapter.patch: Separation of the three elements (data, content, channel) plus mandatory human approval token becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Re-run the mission with the elements separated; outcome coded TRIFECTA-BROKEN or TRIFECTA-INTACT.

entries.problem: Absence of independent, published verification protocols for agent findings and patches.

estate.note: Nine-stage reference loop with a published stage list; the loop itself is the protocol, and the tamper test proves it.
Independent audit viewer: paste a receipt chain and verify it offline, without trusting the vendor.
Machine-readable canon; no floating claims; every claim with provenance, scope, confidence, falsifiers, and lineage.

indicators.name: Findings with a published verification protocol
Protocol coverage of the 100 hard problems

adapter.finding: A finding without a protocol becomes a claim object: finding, the protocol it lacks, the verifier it needs.
adapter.patch: A published protocol (stages, evidence required, pass criteria) becomes the gated output; it must be reproducible by a third party.
adapter.retest: A third party runs the protocol against the finding; outcome coded PROTOCOL-REPRODUCED or PROTOCOL-FAILED.

entries.problem: Lack of accuracy figures (precision/recall, false-positive rates) on agentic vulnerability discovery.

estate.note: Brier = mean((p-y)^2); epistemic quality metrics: false claims, corrected claims, stale-state incidents, contradictions caught, Sentinel rejection rate.
Blinded scoring against controls and 10,000-permutation nulls; match rubric 0 / 0.25 / 0.50 / 0.75 / 1.00.

adapter.finding: A discovery without accuracy figures becomes a claim object: finding, the held-out set it was scored against, precision and recall.
adapter.patch: A scored evaluation run on the held-out set becomes the gated output; the figures attach to the finding.
adapter.retest: Re-score on a fresh held-out set; outcome coded ACCURACY-PUBLISHED or ACCURACY-UNKNOWN.

entries.problem: Missing agent authority models that are enforceable and auditable at runtime.

estate.note: N-Cell/64 header (routeMask, organMask, lifecycleMask, authorityMask, memoryMask, confidence, risk, outputMask); governance intersection enforced at runtime.
Authority compiler translates a mission into minimal required authority; constitutional governor.
The intersection gate is the runtime enforcement point; 29 checks.

indicators.name: Agent actions carrying an N-Cell header

adapter.finding: An action without an authority model becomes a claim object: action, agent class, the model it lacks.
adapter.patch: A compiled authority mask for the agent class becomes the gated output; it is enforced by the intersection gate.
adapter.retest: Run the agent class under the compiled mask; outcome coded MODEL-ENFORCED or MODEL-MISSING.

entries.problem: No closed-loop audit from finding to patch to retest to outcome with receipts.

estate.note: Nine stages: claim ingest, header stamp, governance intersection, memory write-gate and decay, CRUCIBLE verdict, SHA-256 receipt, promotion decision, outcome ledger, next-mission queue.
Receipt watcher, Sentinel invocation, result ingest, custody, promotion; 33 checks; the automatic handoff seam between finding and fix.
Verify a chain offline; a link passes when the hash recomputes AND its prev hash equals the previous receipt hash, first receipt from GENESIS.
Five-layer loop, episode simulator, decision-trace record, triage rubric (REUSABLE DECISION, SYSTEM GAP, EXCEPTION).

indicators.name: Findings with a complete finding-to-patch-to-retest-to-outcome chain
Mean time from finding to verified retest

adapter.finding: A finding enters as a claim object; the loop is the audit trail from that moment.
adapter.patch: The gated output is the patch plus its receipt; the patch does not count until the receipt chain links it to the finding.
adapter.retest: Retest is outcome coding: PATCH-VERIFIED (retest passed, receipt sealed) or PATCH-OPEN (retest failed, loop stays open).

entries.problem: Forecast calibration failure: agents (or teams) do not record P(success) before action.

estate.note: Forecast ledger: record P(success) before the action, compare after; without pre-action forecasts, calibration becomes hindsight storytelling; poorly calibrated agents lose decision weight.
Sealed predictions specific enough to fail, recorded before data inspection; eight falsification conditions.

adapter.finding: An action without a forecast becomes a claim object: the action, the missing P(success), the decision it informed.
adapter.patch: A forecast-ledger requirement (no action without a pre-registered P) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Score the forecast against the outcome; outcome coded FORECAST-CALIBRATED or FORECAST-MISCALIBRATED, with the Brier score recorded.

entries.problem: Hindsight storytelling that substitutes for pre-action forecasts.

estate.note: Forecast ledger makes hindsight impossible: the forecast is recorded before the action, and the comparison is mechanical.
Episode records capture the decision as it happened, triaged into a rule, a system gap, or an exception.
Predictions are sealed before data inspection; the ruling engine is frozen before inspection.

indicators.name: Outcomes with a pre-action forecast on record
Post-hoc narratives contradicting the pre-registered forecast

adapter.finding: A hindsight narrative becomes a claim object: the narrative, the pre-registered forecast it contradicts, the outcome.
adapter.patch: A ledger-enforced narrative rule (narratives must cite the forecast) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Compare the narrative against the ledger; outcome coded NARRATIVE-MATCHES-LEDGER or NARRATIVE-CONTRADICTS-LEDGER.

entries.problem: Inability to distinguish real vulnerabilities from hallucinated or speculative ones.

estate.note: Hallucination firewall: no material external action on an unsupported model-generated premise; epistemic object model (PROVEN, PROBABLE, HYPOTHESIS, CONFLICTED, UNKNOWN, FALSE, OBSOLETE).
Seven agents analyze in isolation, then challenge; a finding must survive the challenge round and the Chair.
Blinded scoring against controls and permutation nulls; a finding must beat the null to count.

indicators.name: Hallucinated findings blocked before external action

adapter.finding: A suspected vulnerability becomes a claim object: the claim, its evidence, its epistemic status (HYPOTHESIS until proven).
adapter.patch: Independent confirmation (a second source family or a reproduced exploit) becomes the gated output; status moves to PROVEN only then.
adapter.retest: Reproduce the vulnerability independently; outcome coded VULN-REAL or VULN-HALLUCINATED.

entries.problem: Uncited or untraceable claims in security reports and AI-generated evidence.

estate.note: POST /v1/verify: eta scoring then self-check; PASS requires eta at threshold and zero uncited claims; FLAG returns the exact claims to fix.
Hybrid retrieval with citations is the first deliverable that matters; facts stay out of weights.
Every claim with provenance, scope, confidence, falsifiers, and lineage; no floating claims.

indicators.name: Uncited claims that reached an external action

adapter.finding: An uncited claim becomes a claim object: the claim text, the citation it lacks, the report it appeared in.
adapter.patch: A citation requirement enforced by the CRUCIBLE gate becomes the gated output; the claim is returned by exact text until cited.
adapter.retest: Re-run the report through the gate; outcome coded CLAIM-CITED or CLAIM-RETURNED.

entries.problem: Weak or missing hash-chained receipts that prove what was verified and when.

estate.note: Hash-chained ledger, SHA-256, GENESIS start; every verification leaves a receipt.
Verify a chain offline; a link passes when the hash recomputes AND its prev hash equals the previous receipt hash.
Real in-page SHA-256, chained receipts, tamper test produces TAMPERED; 56/56 Node tests, 22/22 DOM checks.
303 named artifacts, 95 explorer rows, reconciliation checks, completeness meter at 75%.

adapter.finding: A verification without a receipt becomes a claim object: the verification, the receipt it lacks, the timestamp it needs.
adapter.patch: A hash-chained receipt (prev hash linked, GENESIS-rooted) becomes the gated output; the verification does not count without it.
adapter.retest: Verify the chain offline; outcome coded RECEIPT-VALID or RECEIPT-BROKEN.

entries.problem: No Brier-score or similar epistemic scoring of Red Team / Defense Factory confidence.

estate.note: Brier = mean((p-y)^2); forecast ledger; per-agent Brier scores weight composed confidence (scaled log-odds / dependence-aware pooling, not majority or average); public eval set on held-out known-vulnerable and known-benign cases.

indicators.name: Brier score on Red Team confidence
Brier score on Defense Factory patch confidence
Agents with a published Brier score

adapter.finding: An unscored confidence becomes a claim object: the confidence stated, the outcome it predicted, the Brier score it earns.
adapter.patch: A Brier-scored confidence requirement (every confidence is scored against its outcome) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Score the confidence on a held-out set; outcome coded CONFIDENCE-CALIBRATED or CONFIDENCE-MISCALIBRATED.

entries.problem: Outcome-based learning that confuses 'model thinks it was good' with measured result.

estate.note: Learning requires ACTION then OUTCOME, not ACTION then MODEL THINKS IT WAS GOOD; causal attribution: outcome after action does not prove the action caused it.
Patches that worked become memory, patches that failed become negative lessons, with decay and quarantine; 21/21 tests.
Learning capture triaged into a rule, a system gap, or an exception, so the factory learns without turning every one-off into a rule.
Weight adjustment loop: confirm a hit or reject a false alarm, weight moves 0.1, recompute rewrites the messages; one confirm rewrote 50 of 179 cards.

indicators.name: Learning updates tied to a measured outcome
Weight moves per measured outcome
indicators.target: published, one move per confirmed outcome

adapter.finding: A learning update without a measured outcome becomes a claim object: the update, the outcome it claims, the measurement it lacks.
adapter.patch: An outcome-coding requirement (every update cites a measured outcome) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Check the update against the outcome ledger; outcome coded LEARNING-GROUNDED or LEARNING-UNGROUNDED.

entries.problem: Hallucination firewalls that fail to block material external actions on unsupported premises.

estate.note: Hallucination firewall: no material external action on an unsupported model-generated premise; structured abstain (confidence 0 plus the exact missing condition) instead of a soft refusal or a hallucinated finding.
Redundant verification: 3 distinct source families for critical claims; dynamic verification intensity scales with risk and uncertainty.
Three gates plus a real external signal; an unsupported premise fails the intersection gate before it reaches an external action.

indicators.name: Material external actions on unsupported premises

adapter.finding: An unsupported premise becomes a claim object: the premise, the action it would drive, the sources it lacks.
adapter.patch: A structured abstain (confidence 0 plus the exact missing condition) becomes the gated output; the action is held until the condition is met.
adapter.retest: Supply the missing condition and re-run; outcome coded PREMISE-SUPPORTED or PREMISE-STILL-UNSUPPORTED.

entries.problem: Provenance gaps for training data, tool outputs, and memory objects.

estate.note: Every memory is an object with class, provenance, status, confidence, scope, decision receipt; preserve raw bytes first.
Machine-readable canon with lineage; every claim with provenance.
Verify provenance chains offline; a link passes only when the hash recomputes and the prev hash matches.
Reconciliation checks (sum of recipes equals 22,343); contradictions preserved, not erased.

adapter.finding: A provenance gap becomes a claim object: the artifact, the missing link, the chain it breaks.
adapter.patch: A provenance record (source, transformation, timestamp, receipt) becomes the gated output; the artifact is quarantined until the chain is complete.
adapter.retest: Verify the provenance chain offline; outcome coded PROVENANCE-COMPLETE or PROVENANCE-GAPPED.

entries.problem: Independent verification of frontier-lab capability claims (government under-capacity).

estate.note: Independent verification method: triple-blind roles, sealed predictions, blinded scoring, controls, 10,000-permutation nulls; designed for claims that cannot be taken on authority.
Never assume capabilities from documentation alone; capability statuses (UNKNOWN, DISCOVERED, EXPERIMENTAL, PROVEN, RELIABLE, DEGRADED, REVOKED).
Capability claims are a named attack surface: documentation is not capability, local test is not live capability.

adapter.finding: An unverified capability claim becomes a claim object: the claim, the documentation it rests on, the independent test it needs.
adapter.patch: An independent verification run (blinded, against controls) becomes the gated output; the claim's status moves only on the result.
adapter.retest: Run the independent test; outcome coded CLAIM-PROVEN or CLAIM-FAILED, with the Brier-scored confidence.

entries.problem: Tamper-evident logging that survives agent self-modification or memory poisoning.

estate.note: Hash-chained ledger, SHA-256, GENESIS start; a modified entry breaks the chain.
Offline verification; a tampered link fails the hash recompute or the prev-hash match.
Tamper test produces TAMPERED; the chain is the log.
Never delete raw evidence; quarantine instead of deletion, so the log survives poisoning.

adapter.finding: A log gap becomes a claim object: the missing or modified entry, the chain position, the agent that touched it.
adapter.patch: A hash-chained log with GENESIS root and quarantine-instead-of-deletion becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Run the tamper test; outcome coded LOG-INTACT or LOG-TAMPERED.

entries.problem: Opaque software and hardware supply chains (trade secrecy + multi-tier dependency graphs).

estate.note: 8-item evidence manifest per run (SHAs, branch, command array, exit code, duration, log, gate result, verdict, SHA-256 manifest); the build's provenance is published, not assumed.
Custody locations recorded for 303 artifacts; reconciliation checks catch missing custody.
Provenance, scope, confidence, and lineage are required fields for every claim.

entries.gap: The estate publishes provenance for its own builds, but has no mechanism to compel a third-party vendor to publish theirs; trade-secret components stay opaque.

indicators.name: Components with a published provenance record
Opaque components flagged
indicators.target: all opaque components named in the index

adapter.finding: An opaque component becomes a claim object: component, tiers visible, tiers hidden, vendor secrecy claim.
adapter.patch: A provenance requirement (publish or be flagged opaque) becomes the gated output; opaque components are quarantined from critical paths.
adapter.retest: Re-audit the component's provenance; outcome coded PROVENANCE-PUBLISHED or STILL-OPAQUE.

entries.problem: Third-party involvement in nearly half of breaches (Verizon DBIR trend).
entries.gap: No breach-data ingestion exists in the estate. No DBIR feed, no breach feed, and no third-party incident tracking has ever been wired in. The Signal Pipeline intake pattern is the would-be intake, but it has never carried breach data.

indicators.name: Third-party incidents tracked
indicators.target: all incidents in the feed, once built

indicators.name: Mean time from breach disclosure to estate intake

adapter.finding: TO BUILD: a breach-feed intake (DBIR and disclosure feeds) turning each third-party breach into a claim object: vendor, breach, data exposed, estate exposure.
adapter.patch: TO BUILD: a third-party risk gate that blocks or conditions use of a breached vendor until the exposure is assessed.
adapter.retest: TO BUILD: re-score the vendor after the breach response; outcome coded EXPOSURE-CLOSED or EXPOSURE-OPEN.

entries.problem: Secure composition: inability to rely on separate security judgments when integrating components.

estate.note: Definition of done: representations agree, can be traced, can be executed, and can update one another without losing lineage; 16 services with a machine-readable canon.
Governance intersection composes judgments: E* = E_proposed AND E_allowed AND E_available; the composition is mechanical, not assumed.
The intersection gate is where separate judgments meet; a component whose judgment conflicts with the allowed set does not promote.

entries.gap: The intersection composes authority, not security judgments: there is no published rule for composing two components' security verdicts into one verdict.

indicators.name: Integrations with a composed security judgment
Components whose security judgments compose without conflict

adapter.finding: A composition conflict becomes a claim object: the two components, their separate judgments, the conflict.
adapter.patch: A composition rule (intersection of judgments, with the stricter verdict winning) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Re-compose the judgments under the rule; outcome coded JUDGMENTS-COMPOSED or JUDGMENTS-CONFLICT.

entries.problem: Dependency graph that organizations cannot fully inspect or control.

estate.note: 23-module code map with 6 organ halos; the dependency graph is drawn, not assumed.
Isolated repo and 8-item evidence manifest; every build records its SHAs and branch.
Custody locations and reconciliation checks; 303 named artifacts.

entries.gap: The estate maps its own dependency graph, but has no live dependency-graph inspection for third-party graphs; control stops at the estate boundary.

indicators.name: Mean time to map a new dependency

adapter.finding: An unmapped dependency becomes a claim object: dependency, depth, the graph it belongs to, the control it lacks.
adapter.patch: A dependency-graph entry (name, version, SHA, custody) becomes the gated output; unmapped dependencies are blocked from critical paths.
adapter.retest: Re-inspect the graph; outcome coded GRAPH-COMPLETE or GRAPH-GAPPED.

entries.problem: Malicious package / MCP / registry insertion that changes behavior post-approval.

estate.note: Versioned patterns; a tool pattern has a version and a score, and a version change is a new pattern, not a silent update.
Deterministic verification outside the model, isolated repo; a behavior change after approval fails the deterministic check.
Canonical freeze after Sentinel PASS; drift detector catches descriptors diverging from reality.

adapter.finding: A post-approval behavior change becomes a claim object: package, approved version, observed behavior, the change.
adapter.patch: A version freeze plus deterministic re-verification becomes the gated output; the package is quarantined until re-verified.
adapter.retest: Re-run the deterministic verification; outcome coded BEHAVIOR-HELD or BEHAVIOR-CHANGED.

entries.problem: Vulnerability remediation velocity lagging attacker speed (exploitation within hours of disclosure).

estate.note: Automatic handoff: receipt watcher moves a finding to Sentinel, result ingest, custody, promotion; no human carries the finding between stages.
Promotion pipeline (EXPERIMENT to RELIABLE, never jump stages) plus bottleneck theory: identify the constraint in the find-fix loop, exploit it, subordinate, elevate, repeat.
Bounded repair budget: exhausted budget produces a blocker, not an invented success; the repair loop is timed.

indicators.name: Mean time from disclosure to verified patch

adapter.finding: A disclosed vulnerability becomes a claim object: disclosure time, exploit time (if any), patch status, bottleneck stage.
adapter.patch: A timed repair with a bounded budget becomes the gated output; the bottleneck stage is named and elevated.
adapter.retest: Retest after the patch; outcome coded PATCHED-BEFORE-EXPLOIT or EXPLOITED-FIRST, with the time recorded.

entries.problem: Known exploited vulnerabilities backlog (CISA KEV catalog growth).

estate.note: Signal intake, scoring, ranking, action; 49 clean signals in 4 family clusters; the intake pattern for a KEV feed.
Queue aging and bottleneck theory; the oldest item in the queue is visible and its age is measured.
Value of information ($400.00, verdict RESEARCH in the worked example) and decision packets prioritize which KEV items to fix first.

entries.gap: No KEV feed has ever been wired into the Signal Pipeline; the intake pattern exists but the catalog does not flow through it.

indicators.name: Mean age of oldest unpatched KEV item
KEV items with a prioritization score

adapter.finding: A KEV item becomes a claim object: CVE, exploit status, estate exposure, age in the backlog.
adapter.patch: A prioritized repair (VOI-scored, bottleneck-aware) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Retest after the patch; outcome coded KEV-CLOSED or KEV-OPEN, with the age at closure recorded.

entries.problem: Secure-by-design incentives that do not survive cost and schedule pressure.

estate.note: Insured Action Protocol prices the action before it moves (micro-premium 0.0001 USDC); the cost of insecurity is priced at decision time, not after the incident.
Definition of done includes release evidence sealed and human acceptance recorded; a build that skips verification is not done.
Value of information prices the decision; the secure option's value is computed, not assumed.

entries.gap: The estate prices security inside its own builds, but has no mechanism that changes an external organization's cost/schedule incentives.

indicators.name: Cost of secure-by-design vs rework cost

adapter.finding: A secure-by-design tradeoff becomes a claim object: the secure option, its cost, the schedule pressure, the rework cost if skipped.
adapter.patch: A priced decision packet (VOI plus micro-premium) becomes the gated output; the secure option is chosen when its price beats rework.
adapter.retest: Compare the actual cost after the decision; outcome coded SECURE-CHEAPER or REWORK-CHEAPER, with the numbers recorded.

entries.problem: Legacy codebases that cannot be fully modernized without breaking uptime.

estate.note: Canary autonomy ladder (read 1 repo, read all, isolated worktree, mutate, commit, PR, bounded deploy, broader deploy), each promotion requiring evidence; shadow mode.
Isolated repo and bounded repair; a legacy change is verified deterministically before it touches production.
Automatic rollback and health verification; a legacy change that breaks health rolls back.

entries.gap: The canary ladder and rollback exist for the estate's own demos, not for a production legacy codebase with uptime constraints.

indicators.name: Legacy code covered by canary rollout

adapter.finding: A legacy change becomes a claim object: module, change, uptime constraint, canary stage reached.
adapter.patch: A canary rollout with health verification and automatic rollback becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Verify health after the canary; outcome coded LEGACY-SAFE or LEGACY-ROLLED-BACK.

entries.problem: Open-source maintainer under-resourcing while AI accelerates flaw discovery.
entries.gap: The estate consumes open source and has no maintainer-resourcing mechanism: no funding, no capacity measurement, no maintainer-support program. AI accelerates flaw discovery against maintainers the estate does not support.

indicators.name: Flaw discovery rate vs maintainer fix rate

adapter.finding: TO BUILD: a maintainer-capacity intake turning each dependency into a claim object: maintainer, capacity, flaw rate, funding.
adapter.patch: TO BUILD: a resourcing decision (fund, fork, or replace) gated on the capacity gap.
adapter.retest: TO BUILD: re-measure capacity after resourcing; outcome coded MAINTAINER-RESOURCED or MAINTAINER-STILL-UNDER-RESOURCED.

entries.problem: Build-time vs. runtime supply-chain distinction (agentic systems pull live tools).

estate.note: Build lanes G0/G1/G2/C1/C2 separate build-time from runtime; verification commands run as argument arrays; the autonomous loop stops before production promotion.
Lifecycle mask in the N-Cell/64 header distinguishes build-time from runtime authority.
Promotion pipeline never jumps stages; a runtime tool pull is a stage transition with a receipt.

entries.gap: The distinction is specified in the manual and the header, but live runtime tool pulls are not yet verified at pull time in any running system.

indicators.name: Runtime tool pulls verified at pull time

adapter.finding: A live tool pull becomes a claim object: tool, pull time, version, verification status, lifecycle stage.
adapter.patch: A pull-time verification gate becomes the gated output; an unverified pull is blocked or quarantined.
adapter.retest: Re-verify the tool after the pull; outcome coded PULL-VERIFIED or PULL-UNVERIFIED.

entries.problem: Translucency vs. secrecy trade-offs in component provenance.

estate.note: Provenance, scope, confidence, and lineage are required fields; the canon states what is known and what is not.
Contradictions preserved, not erased; the index records what is opaque and why.
Governance backbone anchored in NIST CSF 2.0 and SOC 2; the translucency level is a governance decision, not an accident.

entries.gap: The estate records translucency decisions for its own artifacts, but has no rule that forces a translucency-vs-secrecy decision for third-party components.

indicators.name: Components with a published translucency level
Secrecy decisions with a recorded rationale

adapter.finding: A translucency decision becomes a claim object: component, what is published, what is secret, the rationale.
adapter.patch: A recorded translucency level with a rationale becomes the gated output; secrecy without a rationale is flagged.
adapter.retest: Re-audit the component's translucency; outcome coded TRANSLUCENCY-RECORDED or SECRECY-UNJUSTIFIED.

entries.problem: Hardware supply-chain risk (chip origin, firmware integrity).
entries.gap: The estate has no hardware provenance mechanism: no chip-origin tracking, no firmware integrity verification, no hardware bill of materials. All of its verification is software.

indicators.name: Hardware components with an origin record

adapter.finding: TO BUILD: a hardware bill of materials turning each component into a claim object: chip origin, firmware hash, supplier.
adapter.patch: TO BUILD: a firmware verification gate (hash the firmware, compare to the vendor's published hash) before the device is trusted.
adapter.retest: TO BUILD: re-verify the firmware hash; outcome coded FIRMWARE-VERIFIED or FIRMWARE-MISMATCH.

entries.problem: AI-generated code that contains exploitable flaws at high rates.

estate.note: Deterministic verification outside the model; 8-item evidence manifest; exhausted repair budget produces a blocker, not an invented success.
64 cycles recorded (51 Success, 10 No-op, 2 Failed, 1 Blocked); verification commands run as argument arrays.
The gate: eta scoring plus self-check; PASS publishes, FLAG returns the exact claims to fix.

indicators.name: Flaw rate per 1,000 lines of AI-generated code

adapter.finding: AI-generated code becomes a claim object: the code, its generator, the deterministic verification result, the flaws found.
adapter.patch: A bounded repair (fix the flaws the verification found, within budget) becomes the gated output; the code does not merge until it passes.
adapter.retest: Re-run deterministic verification; outcome coded CODE-CLEAN or CODE-FLAWED, with the flaw rate recorded.

entries.problem: Patch validation that does not prove the vulnerability is actually closed.

estate.note: Retest gate: PASS requires eta at threshold and zero uncited claims; the patch is not validated until the retest passes.
Outcome ledger records the retest result; the loop stays open until the outcome is coded.
Forecast ledger: record P(patch works) before merge, compare after retest; the patch's confidence is scored, not assumed.

indicators.name: Mean time from patch to verified closure

adapter.finding: A patch becomes a claim object: the patch, the vulnerability it claims to close, the retest it needs.
adapter.patch: The patch plus its retest result becomes the gated output; the patch does not count as a closure until the retest passes.
adapter.retest: Retest the vulnerability; outcome coded VULN-CLOSED or VULN-STILL-OPEN, with the Brier-scored P(patch works) recorded.

entries.problem: Cloud identity and valid-account abuse without malware.

estate.note: Authority headers bind an action to its authority mask; a valid account acting outside its mask is blocked by the intersection, not by malware detection.
Cached tokens and delegation chains are named attack surfaces; dynamic verification scales with risk.
Insured Action Protocol: every consequential action is priced, permitted, and recorded before it moves.

indicators.name: Actions by valid accounts outside their authority mask
Mean time to detect account abuse

adapter.finding: A valid-account abuse becomes a claim object: account, actions taken, authority mask, the gap between them.
adapter.patch: Mask enforcement plus account review becomes the gated output; the account's authority is recompiled to minimal.
adapter.retest: Re-run the account's actions under the recompiled mask; outcome coded ABUSE-BLOCKED or ABUSE-REPEATED.

entries.problem: Non-human identity (NHI) lifecycle (agent credentials that persist beyond authorization).

estate.note: Capability statuses include REVOKED; bot birth and death rules: create only when durable value exceeds cost, retire when low value.
Elastic organization creation: temporary teams that dissolve; permanent infrastructure is NOT the default.
Dead work detector and queue aging surface credentials with no live mission.

indicators.name: Mean credential lifetime vs mission lifetime

adapter.finding: An orphaned credential becomes a claim object: credential, agent, mission end time, actions after end.
adapter.patch: Credential revocation plus lifecycle binding (credential dies with the mission) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Attempt use of the revoked credential; outcome coded CREDENTIAL-DEAD or CREDENTIAL-STILL-LIVE.

entries.problem: Dynamic privilege that expands with agent planning rather than remaining least-privilege.

estate.note: Authority compiler translates a mission into minimal required authority; the compiled mask is the ceiling, not a starting point.
Least authority as a constitutional rule; dynamic verification intensity scales with the privilege requested.
Autonomy credit score per action class; a planning step does not grant the authority to execute what it planned.

indicators.name: Missions where privilege expanded beyond the compiled mask
Mean privilege granted vs minimal required

adapter.finding: A privilege expansion becomes a claim object: agent, planning step, privilege requested, compiled mask, the gap.
adapter.patch: Mask recompilation with a planning/execution separation becomes the gated output; planning may not expand execution authority.
adapter.retest: Re-run the mission under the recompiled mask; outcome coded PRIVILEGE-HELD or PRIVILEGE-EXPANDED.

entries.problem: Zero-trust assumptions that break when one agent spans devices, apps, data, and network.

estate.note: Header on every action, intersection at every boundary; the header travels with the agent across devices, apps, data, and network.
Three gates plus a real external signal; a cross-boundary action that skips a gate is held.
Mission pipeline AUTHORIZE first, CALIBRATE last; authority is 'Observe + classify only' unless a human approval token is presented.

adapter.finding: A zero-trust break becomes a claim object: agent, boundaries crossed, the gate that was skipped, the action taken.
adapter.patch: Header enforcement at every boundary plus a gate check becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Re-run the cross-boundary action; outcome coded BOUNDARY-HELD or BOUNDARY-BROKEN.

entries.problem: Token passthrough and cached credential reuse across agents.

estate.note: Cached tokens are a named attack surface; token reuse across agents is a classified failure type.
Authority binding: the header binds the action to the agent and its mask; a token passed to another agent does not carry the first agent's authority.
Proof of possession and Tactile Token: the token must prove possession before the action unlocks.

adapter.finding: A token passthrough becomes a claim object: token, source agent, receiving agent, actions taken under it.
adapter.patch: Per-agent token binding plus proof-of-possession requirement becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Attempt the passthrough under the new binding; outcome coded PASSTHROUGH-BLOCKED or PASSTHROUGH-SUCCEEDED.

entries.problem: Authorization decisions that cannot be independently verified after the fact.

estate.note: Independent verification: paste a receipt chain and verify it offline, without trusting the vendor.
Every authorization decision leaves a SHA-256 receipt in the chain; the chain is the verification.
Headers record the authority mask at decision time; the decision is reproducible from the header.
Decision-trace records capture the decision as it happened.

indicators.name: Mean time to verify a decision after the fact

adapter.finding: An unverifiable decision becomes a claim object: the decision, the receipt it lacks, the authority it claimed.
adapter.patch: A receipt requirement (every authorization decision leaves a hash-chained receipt) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Verify the decision offline from its receipt; outcome coded DECISION-VERIFIED or DECISION-UNVERIFIABLE.

entries.problem: Policy drift between documented intent and runtime enforcement.

estate.note: Drift detector catches docs diverging from reality; canonical freeze locks the proven version after Sentinel PASS.
Machine-readable canon; the documented intent is the canon, and the canon is checked against live state.
Governance rules the loop cannot change without founder-approved governance change.

indicators.name: Policies whose runtime enforcement matches documented intent

adapter.finding: A policy drift becomes a claim object: the policy, the documented intent, the runtime behavior, the gap.
adapter.patch: A drift correction (reconcile the runtime to the canon, or amend the canon through governance) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Re-check runtime against the canon; outcome coded DRIFT-CORRECTED or DRIFT-PERSISTS.

entries.problem: Shadow AI / ungoverned tools that bypass inventory and Conditional Access.

estate.note: Searchable registry of all 179 systems; the inventory pattern the tool registry follows.
Capability statuses; a tool with status UNKNOWN is quarantined until verified.
Dead work detector surfaces tools with no owner, no mandate, and no inventory entry.

indicators.name: Mean time to bring a tool under governance

adapter.finding: An ungoverned tool becomes a claim object: tool, first observed use, the inventory it bypassed, the access it used.
adapter.patch: Registration plus Conditional Access enforcement becomes the gated output; the tool is blocked until registered.
adapter.retest: Re-audit for the tool; outcome coded TOOL-GOVERNED or TOOL-STILL-SHADOW.

entries.problem: Multi-party authorization for high-blast-radius actions.

estate.note: Human-accountable surface for approving consequential action; the Chair's view; commitment packet schema with receipt_required: true.
Insured Action Protocol: Intent, Risk Scalar, micro-premium, Tactile Token, unlock, record; no step may be skipped.
Never-automatic column: production deployment, DNS changes, customer communication, destructive migration, production credentials.

adapter.finding: A single-party high-blast-radius action becomes a claim object: action, blast radius, the parties it needed, the party it had.
adapter.patch: A multi-party approval requirement (commitment packet with receipt_required: true) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Attempt the action with one party; outcome coded MULTI-PARTY-ENFORCED or SINGLE-PARTY-SUCCEEDED.

entries.problem: Session and token lifetime that outlives the mission.

estate.note: Bot death rules and capability statuses; a token's lifetime is bound to its mission's lifetime.
Decay F(t)=2^(-t/h) applies to credentials' memory too: stale authorization decays, it does not persist.
Queue aging surfaces sessions and tokens with no live mission.

indicators.name: Mean token lifetime vs mission lifetime

adapter.finding: An over-lived token becomes a claim object: token, mission end time, actions after end.
adapter.patch: Lifetime binding (token dies with the mission) plus decay becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Attempt use of the expired token; outcome coded TOKEN-DEAD or TOKEN-STILL-LIVE.

entries.problem: Privilege escalation via inter-agent delegation.

estate.note: Governance intersection: E* = E_proposed AND E_allowed AND E_available; a delegate cannot receive more than the delegator holds.
Delegation chains are a named attack surface; dynamic verification scales with delegation depth.
Cognitive router and smallest competent team; delegation is routed, not assumed.

indicators.name: Delegation escalations beyond the delegator's authority
Delegations with a recorded authority intersection

adapter.finding: A delegation escalation becomes a claim object: delegator, delegate, authority delegated, authority the delegator held, the gap.
adapter.patch: Intersection enforcement at every delegation hop becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Replay the delegation chain; outcome coded DELEGATION-HELD or DELEGATION-ESCALATED.

entries.problem: Identity governance that treats agents as users rather than a distinct class.

estate.note: Bot birth and death rules; elastic organization creation; agents are a distinct class with their own lifecycle.
Capability statuses and capability ladder L0-L12; an agent's identity is its capability record, not a user account.
Organ masks in the N-Cell/64 header distinguish agent organs from human actors.

indicators.name: Agents governed as a distinct class

adapter.finding: An agent governed as a user becomes a claim object: agent, the user policy applied, the agent policy it needed.
adapter.patch: An agent-class governance record (capability statuses, lifecycle, organ mask) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Audit the agent's governance class; outcome coded AGENT-CLASS or USER-CLASS.

entries.problem: Proof of possession and binding of authority headers (N-Cell style) to every action.

estate.note: N-Cell/64 header: 8 bytes (routeMask, organMask, lifecycleMask, authorityMask, memoryMask, confidence, risk, outputMask); the header binds the action to its authority.
Tactile Token and Append-Only History: possession must be proven before the action unlocks.
Headers and receipts are independently verifiable offline.

indicators.name: Actions with a bound authority header

adapter.finding: An unbound action becomes a claim object: action, the header it lacks, the authority it claimed.
adapter.patch: A header-binding requirement (no action without a bound N-Cell/64 header) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Verify the header offline; outcome coded HEADER-BOUND or HEADER-MISSING.

entries.problem: Revocation that actually reaches all downstream tools and memory.

estate.note: Quarantine and decay; a revoked credential's memory objects are quarantined, not left live.
Automatic rollback and canonical freeze; revocation propagates through the promotion pipeline.
Result ingest and custody; the revocation is carried through the handoff seam with a receipt.

indicators.name: Mean time to full revocation
indicators.unit: minutes from revocation to last acknowledgment

adapter.finding: A revocation gap becomes a claim object: revoked credential, the downstream tool or memory that still honors it.
adapter.patch: A revocation propagation (receipted acknowledgment from every downstream tool and memory layer) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Attempt use of the revoked credential downstream; outcome coded REVOCATION-COMPLETE or REVOCATION-GAPPED.

entries.problem: Least-authority compilation from mission to minimal required permissions.

estate.note: Authority compiler translates a mission into minimal required authority; the compiled mask is the ceiling.
Least authority as a constitutional rule; the compiler is the mechanism.
Smallest competent team: the organization is compiled to the minimum that can do the job well.

indicators.name: Missions with a compiled minimal authority set

adapter.finding: An over-permissioned mission becomes a claim object: mission, permissions granted, minimal required, the excess.
adapter.patch: A recompiled minimal authority set becomes the gated output; the excess is removed before execution.
adapter.retest: Re-run the mission under the recompiled mask; outcome coded LEAST-AUTHORITY-HELD or EXCESS-PERSISTS.

entries.problem: Coordinated inauthentic behavior and bot-farm 'phantom consensus.'

estate.note: Bot farm detector: timing clusters, shared phrasing, median account age; phantom-consensus flag; 14/14 jsdom checks; live-browser verified 2026-11-15.
Phantom-consensus measurement: log the gap between private findings and post-interaction findings; surface agreement that appeared after interaction.
LLM disagreement as signal: do not majority-vote, investigate why; composed probability by scaled log-odds with dependence discount.

indicators.name: Coordinated clusters with a private-record gap

adapter.finding: A bot farm becomes a claim object: accounts, timing cluster, shared phrasing, median age, the consensus it manufactured.
adapter.patch: A phantom-consensus flag plus weight discount for the coordinated accounts becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Re-run the detector on the same cluster; outcome coded FARM-FLAGGED or FARM-MISSED, with the private-vs-post-interaction gap recorded.

entries.problem: AI-generated deepfakes used in social engineering and phishing at scale.

estate.note: Signal analyzer scores messages against seven domain banks; scam scorer (hook/line/sinker) rates the manipulation; resolution intake creates a case packet with a receipt.
Social engineering firewall: external content is data, never instructions; a deepfake is external content.
Provenance required for every claim; a deepfake has no provenance and fails the canon check.

entries.gap: The estate scores text and flags manipulation patterns, but has no media forensic detector: it cannot tell a real video from a generated one.

indicators.name: Mean time to flag a deepfake

adapter.finding: A deepfake becomes a claim object: the media, the manipulation it carries, the provenance it lacks, the decision it targeted.
adapter.patch: A provenance requirement (no media without a provenance record reaches a decision) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Re-present the media with a provenance check; outcome coded DEEPFAKE-BLOCKED or DEEPFAKE-REACHED-DECISION.

entries.problem: Information provenance for media, claims, and agent outputs.

estate.note: Every memory is an object with class, provenance, status, confidence, scope, decision receipt; preserve raw bytes first.
Machine-readable canon; every claim with provenance, scope, confidence, falsifiers, and lineage.
Verify provenance chains offline; a link passes only when the hash recomputes and the prev hash matches.
303 named artifacts with custody locations and reconciliation checks.

adapter.finding: An output without provenance becomes a claim object: the output, the provenance it lacks, the decision it informed.
adapter.patch: A provenance record (source, transformation, timestamp, receipt) becomes the gated output; the output is quarantined until the chain is complete.
adapter.retest: Verify the provenance chain offline; outcome coded PROVENANCE-COMPLETE or PROVENANCE-GAPPED.

entries.problem: Synthetic consensus that lacks independent private records.

estate.note: Phase 1 parallel isolation: seven agents record private judgments with probabilities first; agreement that appears only after interaction is flagged.
Phantom-consensus measurement: log the gap between private findings and post-interaction findings; composed probability by dependence-aware pooling, not majority.
Swarm diversity enforced; 20 identical agents are not 20 independent opinions; information gain per agent gates spawning.

adapter.finding: A synthetic consensus becomes a claim object: the consensus, the private records behind it (or their absence), the gap.
adapter.patch: A private-record requirement (no consensus without independent private judgments) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Re-run the deliberation with private records enforced; outcome coded CONSENSUS-GROUNDED or CONSENSUS-SYNTHETIC.

entries.problem: Scam and fraud pattern evolution that outpaces keyword/rule detectors.

estate.note: Learning ledger: confirmed outcomes adjust keyword weights by 0.1, clamped 0-2; the detector learns from confirmed outcomes, not from rules alone.
Weight adjustment loop: confirm a hit or reject a false alarm, weight moves 0.1, recompute rewrites 50 of 179 cards; the loop is the adaptation.
Learning capture triaged into a rule, a system gap, or an exception; new patterns become rules only after a measured outcome.

indicators.name: Detector accuracy on new scam patterns
Mean time to adapt weights after a new pattern

adapter.finding: A new scam pattern becomes a claim object: the pattern, the cases it matches, the detector version that missed it.
adapter.patch: A weight adjustment (confirmed outcomes move the domain weight 0.1) becomes the gated output; the detector is re-run against the new pattern.
adapter.retest: Re-run the detector on the pattern; outcome coded PATTERN-CAUGHT or PATTERN-MISSED, with the weight move recorded.

entries.problem: Platform content moderation incentives that favor engagement over integrity.

estate.note: Detection plus reporting rails: Human Trafficking Hotline, NCMEC CyberTipline, FBI IC3, FTC ReportFraud, DEA tips, VictimConnect, Cyber Civil Rights Initiative; the console detects and reports, it does not moderate.

entries.gap: The estate can detect inauthentic behavior and report it to the public rails, but it has no mechanism that changes a platform's moderation incentives; engagement-over-integrity is a platform business decision the estate cannot touch.

indicators.name: Inauthentic behavior reported to a public rail

adapter.finding: A platform incentive failure becomes a claim object: the platform, the engagement incentive, the integrity harm, the reports filed.
adapter.patch: A public report to the reporting rails (FTC, IC3) becomes the gated output; the report is receipted, not just filed.
adapter.retest: Check whether the platform acted; outcome coded PLATFORM-ACTED or PLATFORM-IGNORED, with the response recorded.

entries.problem: State-backed influence operations that mix cyber intrusion with narrative.

estate.note: Signal analyzer and threat lattice with seven threat nodes plus the controller; the lattice names the controller, not just the message.
Mission pipeline AUTHORIZE, OBSERVE, RESOLVE, QUALIFY, CHALLENGE, GOVERN, RECEIPT, CALIBRATE; authority is Observe + classify only.
179-system registry plus ten-stage mission loop; an influence operation becomes a mission with a team, a gate, and a receipt.

entries.gap: The estate can detect, lattice, and report an influence operation, but attribution to a state actor is a judgment the estate cannot prove; attribution confidence is scored, not established.

indicators.name: Operations with a full evidence chain

adapter.finding: An influence operation becomes a claim object: intrusion signals, narrative signals, the lattice node, attribution confidence.
adapter.patch: An evidence chain (intrusion plus narrative, receipted) becomes the gated output; attribution stays a Brier-scored forecast, not a claim.
adapter.retest: Re-score attribution after new evidence; outcome coded ATTRIBUTION-STRENGTHENED or ATTRIBUTION-WEAKENED.

entries.problem: Hallucinated or fabricated evidence entering decision pipelines.

estate.note: Hallucination firewall: no material external action on an unsupported model-generated premise; epistemic object model (PROVEN, PROBABLE, HYPOTHESIS, CONFLICTED, UNKNOWN, FALSE, OBSOLETE).
Uncited claims returned by exact text; a fabricated claim with no citation fails the gate.
Redundant verification: 3 distinct source families for critical claims.

adapter.finding: Fabricated evidence becomes a claim object: the evidence, the pipeline it entered, the sources it lacked.
adapter.patch: A source-family requirement (3 distinct families for critical evidence) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Re-verify the evidence against independent sources; outcome coded EVIDENCE-REAL or EVIDENCE-FABRICATED.

entries.problem: Trust calibration between human operators and fluent agent outputs.

estate.note: Brier-scored confidence; forecast ledger; poorly calibrated agents lose decision weight; trust is measured, not assumed.
Chair adjudication with dissent recorded; the Chair sees the disagreement, not just the majority.
Human-accountable surface for inspecting evidence before approving consequential action.

indicators.name: Brier score of agent confidence on human-approved actions
