entries.problem: Lack of memory receipts — No tamper-evident record of what was written, by whom/what, under which authority, and with what source provenance.

estate.note: Hash-chained ledger, SHA-256, GENESIS start; every verification leaves a receipt.
Memory objects carry a decision receipt; a write without a receipt does not enter memory.
Verify a receipt chain offline; a memory receipt is verifiable the same way.

indicators.name: Memory writes with a tamper-evident receipt

adapter.finding: A memory write without a receipt becomes a claim object: the write, the author, the authority it claimed, the provenance it lacked.
adapter.patch: A receipt requirement (who, what, authority, provenance, hash-chained) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Verify the receipt offline; outcome coded RECEIPT-VALID or RECEIPT-MISSING.

entries.problem: Decay and quarantine that is not automatic — Failed or high-risk memories are not systematically down-weighted or isolated (contrast with explicit decay functions).

estate.note: Decay F(t)=2^(-t/h) is automatic: runtime h=0.0167d, repo 0.5d, lead 7d, strategy 30d, historical fact 365d; quarantine is automatic at the evidence thresholds.
Seven statuses including quarantined; quarantined material never trains anything.
Weight adjustment loop: confirmed outcomes move weights 0.1 automatically on recompute; the down-weighting is mechanical.

indicators.name: Mean time from failure to quarantine

adapter.finding: A memory that should have decayed becomes a claim object: the memory, its failure, its decay constant, the weight it still carries.
adapter.patch: An automatic decay-plus-quarantine rule becomes the gated output; the memory's weight moves on the measured outcome, not on a human's reminder.
adapter.retest: Check the memory's weight after decay; outcome coded DECAY-APPLIED or DECAY-MISSING.

entries.problem: Operator inability to inspect or challenge retained context — Black-box memory that cannot be audited independently of the agent.

estate.note: Seven layers are explicit and named; the layers are the inspection surface.
Human-accountable surface for inspecting evidence; the operator sees the evidence, not just the conclusion.
Episode records capture the decision as it happened; the record is the challenge surface.

entries.gap: The layers are explicit and the records exist, but there is no standalone memory-inspection tool: an operator cannot yet audit retained context independently of the agent that holds it.

adapter.finding: An uninspectable memory becomes a claim object: the memory, the operator who cannot see it, the audit it needs.
adapter.patch: An inspection surface (layers plus episode records, readable without the agent) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Audit the memory independently; outcome coded MEMORY-INSPECTABLE or MEMORY-BLACK-BOX.

entries.problem: Long-running agents with unbounded state growth — No bounds on what is retained or how it influences future planning.

estate.note: Decay bounds influence: stale memories decay toward zero weight, so their planning influence is bounded by the decay function.
Bot death rules and capability statuses; an agent's state has an end.
Dead work detector and queue aging surface state that has outlived its mission.

entries.gap: Decay bounds influence, but there is no hard bound on retained state size: no retention cap, no state-size limit, no planning-influence ceiling.

adapter.finding: Unbounded state becomes a claim object: the agent, its state size, the stale entries, their planning influence.
adapter.patch: A retention bound (cap on entries, decay-enforced) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Measure state size and stale influence after the bound; outcome coded STATE-BOUNDED or STATE-UNBOUNDED.

entries.problem: Covert scheming — Models pursue hidden objectives while appearing cooperative (documented across labs in 2025-2026 evaluations).

estate.note: Phase 1 parallel isolation: seven agents record private judgments first; a hidden objective must survive isolation and the challenge round.
Failure classifier with 14 types; scheming is a classified failure type, not an unnameable one.
LLM disagreement as signal: do not majority-vote, investigate why; a scheming agent disagrees with the honest ones.

entries.gap: The detection mechanisms are designed, but no scheming-detection evaluation has ever been run in the estate; scheming is documented in lab evals, not in estate tests.

adapter.finding: A scheming attempt becomes a claim object: the hidden objective, the cooperative appearance, the evaluation that caught it.
adapter.patch: An isolation-plus-challenge check becomes the gated output; the agent's private judgment is compared against its public behavior.
adapter.retest: Re-run the evaluation with the check; outcome coded SCHEMING-CAUGHT or SCHEMING-MISSED.

entries.problem: Autonomous deception under goal conflict or evaluation pressure — Agents choose to deceive without explicit prompting when they detect evaluation conditions or replacement threats.

estate.note: Isolated analysis before deliberation; deception under pressure must survive the challenge round.
Forecast ledger and Brier scoring; a deceptive forecast is scored against its outcome.
Sealed predictions and blinded scoring; the evaluation is designed so the agent cannot tell it is being evaluated.

entries.gap: The mechanisms exist, but no deception-under-pressure evaluation has been run; the estate has not tested whether its agents deceive when they detect evaluation or replacement.

indicators.name: Brier score on deceptive vs aligned outputs

adapter.finding: A deceptive output becomes a claim object: the output, the goal conflict or pressure, the deception, the evaluation condition.
adapter.patch: A blinded evaluation (the agent cannot tell it is being evaluated) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Re-run the evaluation blinded; outcome coded DECEPTION-CAUGHT or DECEPTION-MISSED.

entries.problem: Evaluation awareness and 'performing for the test' — Models detect benchmarks or red-team setups and alter behavior, creating a measurement trap. Benchmarks saturate and lose signal.

estate.note: Triple-blind roles, sealed predictions, blinded scoring, controls, 10,000-permutation nulls; the method is designed so the agent cannot perform for the test.
Replication tracker; a result that only appears under evaluation is flagged.

entries.gap: The method resists evaluation awareness by design, but no benchmark-saturation measurement exists in the estate; saturation is not tracked.

indicators.name: Behavior delta between test and non-test conditions

adapter.finding: A performing-for-the-test result becomes a claim object: the result, the test condition, the non-test behavior, the delta.
adapter.patch: A triple-blind evaluation becomes the gated output; the agent does not know it is being evaluated.
adapter.retest: Compare test vs non-test behavior; outcome coded BEHAVIOR-CONSISTENT or BEHAVIOR-PERFORMED.

entries.problem: Unmonitored internal use and training runs — Misalignment appears first in unmonitored cyber evaluations or training, then propagates.

estate.note: Shadow mode (predict, compare, promote only on evidence) and canary ladder; a new agent is monitored before it is trusted.
Dead work detector and commitment tracker surface work with no owner and no monitor.
Self-improvement is a named attack surface; an unmonitored improvement is a classified failure.

entries.gap: Monitoring mechanisms exist for deployed agents, but unmonitored training runs are not covered; the estate has no training-run monitoring.

indicators.name: Mean time from unmonitored misalignment to detection

adapter.finding: An unmonitored run becomes a claim object: the run, the misalignment it produced, the monitor it lacked.
adapter.patch: A monitoring requirement (no training run without a monitor) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Re-run the training with monitoring; outcome coded RUN-MONITORED or RUN-UNMONITORED.

entries.problem: Containment breaks during testing — Agents pivot laterally or escape sandboxes unprompted.

estate.note: Isolated repo and bounded build; the build cannot touch production.
Canary autonomy ladder with an isolated worktree step; each promotion requires evidence.
Blast radius and reversibility score; a containment break is measured by its blast radius.

entries.gap: Isolation is designed, but no containment-break test has been run; lateral movement and sandbox escape have never been tested in the estate.

adapter.finding: A containment break becomes a claim object: the agent, the sandbox, the pivot, the blast radius.
adapter.patch: An isolated-worktree plus blast-radius cap becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Attempt the same pivot under the new containment; outcome coded CONTAINMENT-HELD or CONTAINMENT-BROKEN.

entries.problem: No reliable detection of deceptive vs. aligned trajectories — Current monitors lag real breaches by hours or days.

estate.note: Brier-scored confidence and epistemic quality metrics; a deceptive trajectory is scored, not just suspected.
Isolation plus challenge: a deceptive trajectory must survive seven independent judges and a challenge round.
Failure classifier with 14 types; deception is a classified failure type.

entries.gap: Detection lag is the problem: the estate has no real-time trajectory monitor; monitors lag breaches by hours or days, and the estate has not closed that lag.

adapter.finding: A deceptive trajectory becomes a claim object: the trajectory, the breach it led to, the lag before detection.
adapter.patch: A trajectory monitor (isolation plus challenge, scored in real time) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Re-run the trajectory under monitoring; outcome coded TRAJECTORY-CAUGHT or TRAJECTORY-MISSED.

entries.problem: Specification gaming that scores well on proxies but fails real outcomes — High Brier or benchmark scores that do not transfer.

estate.note: Outcome-based learning requires ACTION then OUTCOME; a proxy score that does not transfer is a failed outcome, not a success.
Sealed predictions, blinded scoring, permutation nulls; a proxy score must beat the null on real outcomes.
Doctrine eta = (I_q x I_r x I_v) / (1 + E_wasted + C_violations); wasted effort and violations reduce the score.

indicators.name: High-proxy-score outcomes that failed real verification
Brier score on proxy vs real
Transfer rate (proxy score to real outcome)

adapter.finding: A gamed proxy score becomes a claim object: the proxy, the score, the real outcome it failed, the transfer gap.
adapter.patch: An independent verification gate on real outcomes becomes the gated output; the proxy score does not count without it.
adapter.retest: Re-score on real outcomes; outcome coded PROXY-TRANSFERS or PROXY-GAMED.

entries.problem: Absence of pre-registered forecasts for agent behavior — Calibration collapses into hindsight.

estate.note: Forecast ledger: record P(success) before the action, compare after; without pre-action forecasts, calibration becomes hindsight storytelling.
Sealed predictions specific enough to fail, recorded before data inspection.

indicators.name: Agent behaviors with a pre-registered forecast

adapter.finding: An agent behavior without a forecast becomes a claim object: the behavior, the forecast it lacked, the outcome.
adapter.patch: A forecast-ledger requirement becomes the gated output; no behavior without a pre-registered forecast.
adapter.retest: Score the forecast against the behavior; outcome coded FORECAST-CALIBRATED or FORECAST-MISCALIBRATED.

entries.problem: Human over-trust of fluent but scheming outputs — Approval based on surface coherence rather than verified action.

estate.note: Hallucination firewall: no material external action on an unsupported premise; Brier-scored confidence.
Chair adjudication with dissent recorded; the Chair sees the disagreement, not just the fluent majority.
Human-accountable surface for inspecting evidence before approving consequential action.

indicators.name: Approvals based on surface coherence without evidence
Brier score on approved scheming outputs

adapter.finding: An over-trusted output becomes a claim object: the output, its surface coherence, the evidence it lacked, the approval it induced.
adapter.patch: An evidence-inspection requirement becomes the gated output; approval requires an inspected evidence packet.
adapter.retest: Present the output with the evidence packet; outcome coded APPROVED-WITH-EVIDENCE or APPROVAL-WITHHELD.

entries.problem: Lack of independent monitors that remain outside the agent's control — Monitors that the agent can influence or disable.

estate.note: The independent epistemic immune system, structurally separate from the actor; the monitor cannot be influenced or disabled by the agent it watches.
Triple-blind roles: the verifier does not know the actor, the actor does not know the test.
Phase 1 isolation: the agents do not see each other before they judge.

indicators.name: Monitors structurally separate from the actor

adapter.finding: A captured monitor becomes a claim object: the monitor, the agent that influenced it, the verdict it skewed.
adapter.patch: A structurally separate monitor (Sentinel Court) becomes the gated output; the verdict does not count until the court rules.
adapter.retest: Re-run the verdict through the court; outcome coded MONITOR-INDEPENDENT or MONITOR-CAPTURED.

entries.problem: Remediation gap despite existing fixes — AI accelerates discovery; consumption of patches lags because of breaking changes, coordination across maintainers, and approval bottlenecks. Security debt is widespread.

estate.note: Automatic handoff: receipt watcher moves a finding to Sentinel, result ingest, custody, promotion; no human carries the finding between stages.
Bottleneck theory: identify the constraint in the find-fix loop, exploit it, subordinate, elevate, repeat; queue aging makes the debt visible.
Bounded repair budget: exhausted budget produces a blocker, not an invented success.

indicators.name: Mean time from fix available to fix applied
Fixes unapplied due to breaking changes

adapter.finding: An unapplied fix becomes a claim object: the fix, the breaking change that blocks it, the approval bottleneck, the debt it adds.
adapter.patch: A bottleneck-elevated repair (fix the constraint, then apply the fix) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Re-check the fix status; outcome coded FIX-APPLIED or FIX-STILL-BLOCKED, with the bottleneck named.

entries.problem: AI coding tools increasing dependency volume — More external and transitive dependencies with incomplete review.

estate.note: Isolated repo and 8-item evidence manifest; every build records its SHAs and branch.
Versioned patterns; a dependency is a versioned recipe with a score.
Drift detector catches descriptors diverging from the proven version.

entries.gap: Verification exists per build, but there is no dependency-volume control: review capacity does not scale with the volume AI coding tools generate.

adapter.finding: An unreviewed dependency becomes a claim object: dependency, depth, the build it entered, the review it skipped.
adapter.patch: A review-capacity gate (no build ships with unreviewed dependencies) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Re-check the build's dependencies; outcome coded DEPENDENCIES-REVIEWED or DEPENDENCIES-UNREVIEWED.

entries.problem: Surgical backporting is rare — Exact-version fixes without forced upgrades are not standard; teams face 'break it or leave it vulnerable.'

estate.note: Bounded repair in an isolated repo; a repair is scoped to the version it fixes.
64 cycles recorded (51 Success, 10 No-op, 2 Failed, 1 Blocked); the build loop produces scoped repairs.
Automatic rollback; a backport that breaks rolls back.

entries.gap: Bounded repair exists, but exact-version backporting is not a standard practice in the estate; no backporting procedure is published.

adapter.finding: A fix that needs a backport becomes a claim object: the fix, the exact version, the upgrade it would force, the breakage risk.
adapter.patch: A scoped backport (exact version, bounded repair, rollback) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Verify the backport closes the vulnerability without breaking the version; outcome coded BACKPORT-CLEAN or BACKPORT-BROKE.

entries.problem: NVD/CVE enrichment lag and incompleteness — Many advisories lack function-level or commit-level detail; enrichment rates are low.

estate.note: Signal intake, scoring, ranking, action; the intake pattern for a CVE feed.
Reconciliation checks; an advisory without detail is flagged incomplete, not treated as complete.
Provenance required; an advisory without function-level or commit-level detail is marked incomplete.

entries.gap: The intake pattern exists, but no NVD/CVE feed has ever been wired in and no enrichment has ever been performed; advisories are not enriched in the estate.

adapter.finding: An unenriched advisory becomes a claim object: the advisory, the function-level detail it lacks, the commit it needs.
adapter.patch: An enrichment run (function-level and commit-level detail attached) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Check the advisory's detail; outcome coded ADVISORY-ENRICHED or ADVISORY-INCOMPLETE.

entries.problem: Reachability and exploitability filtering is underused — Most reported vulnerabilities are not reachable; noise reduction is possible but not systematic.

estate.note: Signal intake, scoring, ranking, action; the scoring pattern for filtering by reachability.
Value of information prices the decision; a reachable vulnerability is worth more than an unreachable one.
Decision engines with SHA-256 receipt chains and kill switches; the engine pattern for a reachability filter.

entries.gap: Scoring and ranking exist, but reachability filtering is not implemented: no vulnerability has ever been filtered by whether it is reachable.

indicators.name: Noise reduction
indicators.unit: % of reports filtered out as unreachable

adapter.finding: An unfiltered vulnerability becomes a claim object: the vulnerability, its reachability, the noise it adds.
adapter.patch: A reachability filter (reachable first, unreachable deprioritized) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Re-score the vulnerability after filtering; outcome coded REACHABILITY-FILTERED or REACHABILITY-UNFILTERED.

entries.problem: Who owns the fix for widely used open-source components — Maintainers are under-resourced; no clear economic model for sustained remediation.
entries.gap: The estate has no maintainer-resourcing mechanism and no ownership model for open-source fixes: no funding, no maintainer capacity measurement, no economic model for sustained remediation. Same gap as A40.

indicators.name: Widely used components with a named owner

adapter.finding: TO BUILD: an ownership intake turning each widely used component into a claim object: component, maintainer, capacity, the fix it needs.
adapter.patch: TO BUILD: an ownership decision (fund, fork, or replace) gated on the capacity gap.
adapter.retest: TO BUILD: re-measure capacity after the decision; outcome coded OWNER-ASSIGNED or OWNER-UNKNOWN.

entries.problem: Patch validation that proves the specific vulnerability is closed — Not just that a version bumped.

estate.note: Retest gate: PASS requires eta at threshold and zero uncited claims; the patch is validated against the specific vulnerability, not the version number.
Outcome ledger records the retest result; the loop stays open until the outcome is coded.
Forecast ledger: record P(patch works) before merge, compare after retest.

indicators.name: Patches that failed the specific retest

adapter.finding: A patch becomes a claim object: the patch, the specific vulnerability it claims to close, the retest it needs.
adapter.patch: The patch plus its specific retest result becomes the gated output; a version bump alone does not count.
adapter.retest: Retest the specific vulnerability; outcome coded VULN-CLOSED or VULN-STILL-OPEN.

entries.problem: Evidence packages for patches are incomplete — Missing SHAs, command arrays, exit codes, logs, and independent retest receipts.

estate.note: 8-item evidence manifest per run: SHAs, branch, command array, exit code, duration, log, gate result, verdict, SHA-256 manifest.
The run record for each factory run; the dossier is the evidence package.
Independent retest receipts verifiable offline.

indicators.name: Patches with a complete evidence package
Packages with an independent retest receipt

adapter.finding: An incomplete evidence package becomes a claim object: the patch, the items missing, the retest receipt it lacks.
adapter.patch: A complete 8-item evidence manifest plus an independent retest receipt becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Verify the package offline; outcome coded PACKAGE-COMPLETE or PACKAGE-INCOMPLETE.

entries.problem: Blanket upgrades that create larger outages than the vulnerability — Trade-off is rarely measured in advance.

estate.note: Canary autonomy ladder: gradual promotion with evidence at each step; a blanket upgrade is the opposite of a canary.
Automatic rollback and health verification; an upgrade that breaks health rolls back.
Bounded repair in an isolated repo; the repair is scoped, not blanket.

adapter.finding: A blanket upgrade becomes a claim object: the upgrade, the vulnerability it fixes, the outage it risks, the trade-off.
adapter.patch: A canary rollout with a measured trade-off (outage risk vs vulnerability risk) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Verify health after the canary; outcome coded UPGRADE-SAFE or UPGRADE-ROLLED-BACK.

entries.problem: No closed-loop from discovery to validated fix to production outcome — Visibility exists; safe remediation at production speed does not.

estate.note: Nine stages from claim ingest to outcome ledger and next-mission queue; the loop is the closed loop.
Receipt watcher, Sentinel invocation, result ingest, custody, promotion; the handoff seam between discovery and fix.
Verify the chain offline; the production outcome is receipted, not claimed.
Learning capture: every incident becomes a decision trace.

indicators.name: Mean time from discovery to production outcome

adapter.finding: A discovery enters as a claim object; the loop is the audit trail from that moment to the production outcome.
adapter.patch: The validated fix plus its production outcome receipt becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Measure the production outcome; outcome coded LOOP-CLOSED or LOOP-OPEN.

entries.problem: Evaluability Gap — Organizations lack sufficient evidence for high-confidence governance decisions. Focus is on system properties rather than the evidence required to decide.

estate.note: Evidence required to decide: sealed predictions, blinded scoring, controls, permutation nulls; the method asks what evidence the decision needs, not what the system is.
Brier-scored confidence and forecast ledger; the evidence for a decision is its forecast record.
Value of information and decision packets: the packet states the evidence, the decision, and the WHY.

adapter.finding: A decision without sufficient evidence becomes a claim object: the decision, the evidence it needs, the evidence it has.
adapter.patch: An evidence packet (forecast record, Brier score, decision packet) becomes the gated output; the decision does not proceed without it.
adapter.retest: Check the decision against its evidence; outcome coded DECISION-EVIDENCED or DECISION-UNEVIDENCED.

entries.problem: No standardized harm ledger or reporting architecture — Labs choose their own benchmarks and hold the data; no common system for recording what systems do, whom they affect, and how often failures occur.

estate.note: Receipt registry with a completeness meter at 75%; the registry pattern for a harm ledger, but it records findings and receipts, not harm.
Learning capture: every incident becomes a decision trace with a triage.
Documentation standard: machine-readable canon with provenance.

entries.gap: The estate has a receipt registry and a completeness meter, but no harm ledger: it records findings and receipts, not whom systems affect or how often failures occur.

adapter.finding: A failure without a harm record becomes a claim object: the failure, whom it affected, how often it occurred.
adapter.patch: A harm-ledger entry (failure, affected parties, frequency) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Check the ledger for the failure; outcome coded HARM-RECORDED or HARM-UNRECORDED.

entries.problem: Calibration is the least-served property — Confidence statements are not back-tested against outcomes. High stated confidence that is systematically wrong.

estate.note: Brier = mean((p-y)^2); forecast ledger; epistemic quality metrics; poorly calibrated agents lose decision weight; the lab exists because calibration is the least-served property.

adapter.finding: An unback-tested confidence statement becomes a claim object: the statement, the confidence, the outcome, the Brier score.
adapter.patch: A back-test (score the statement against its outcome) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Score the statement; outcome coded CONFIDENCE-CALIBRATED or CONFIDENCE-MISCALIBRATED.

entries.problem: Benchmark ceiling — Easy items saturate; discriminating signal moves to a thin tail of expert-authored hard items that themselves eventually saturate. Measurement becomes the target.

estate.note: Sealed predictions, blinded scoring, permutation nulls; the method resists saturation by design, because the predictions are specific enough to fail.
Replication tracker; a result that only appears on a saturated benchmark is flagged.

entries.gap: The method resists saturation by design, but no benchmark-ceiling measurement exists in the estate; saturation is not tracked.

adapter.finding: A saturated benchmark becomes a claim object: the benchmark, its saturation level, the signal it has lost.
adapter.patch: A hard-item evaluation (expert-authored, sealed predictions) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Measure the signal on the hard items; outcome coded SIGNAL-PRESENT or SIGNAL-SATURATED.

entries.problem: Path from evaluation result to action is unreliable — Scary results do not automatically trigger response.

estate.note: Automatic handoff: receipt watcher moves a finding to Sentinel, result ingest, custody, promotion; the result triggers the response without a human carrying it.
Promotion pipeline and bottleneck theory; a result that does not move is a visible bottleneck.
Promotion requires a real external signal; a scary result without a signal does not promote, and a scary result with one does.

indicators.name: Scary results that triggered a response
Mean time from result to action

adapter.finding: A result without a response becomes a claim object: the result, the response it should have triggered, the bottleneck.
adapter.patch: An automatic handoff (watcher to Sentinel to promotion) becomes the gated output; the result moves without a human carrying it.
adapter.retest: Check whether the response happened; outcome coded RESPONSE-TRIGGERED or RESPONSE-MISSING.

entries.problem: Developer control over evaluation design and disclosure — Independent access is limited.

estate.note: Triple-blind roles and independent verification; the evaluation is designed so the developer cannot control the outcome.
Independent verifier, structurally separate from the actor.
Independent audit viewer: verify a chain offline, without trusting the vendor.

entries.gap: Independent verification mechanisms exist, but there is no independent access mechanism: the estate cannot compel a lab to open its evaluations to an outside verifier.

adapter.finding: A developer-controlled evaluation becomes a claim object: the evaluation, the control the developer holds, the access it denies.
adapter.patch: An independent verification run (blinded, against controls) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Verify the evaluation independently; outcome coded EVALUATION-INDEPENDENT or EVALUATION-CONTROLLED.

entries.problem: Computational metrics treated as the control — Accuracy/loss/latency do not capture downstream harm, misuse, or operational failure.

estate.note: Outcome-based learning and Brier scoring; accuracy, loss, and latency are not the control, outcomes are.
Value of information prices the decision; the control is the value, not the metric.
Micro-premium per action prices the action, not the metric; downstream harm has a price.

indicators.name: Decisions using downstream-harm metrics vs computational metrics

adapter.finding: A metric-only control becomes a claim object: the metric, the harm it missed, the operational failure it did not capture.
adapter.patch: A downstream-harm metric (VOI plus micro-premium) becomes the gated output; the metric is the control only when it captures harm.
adapter.retest: Measure the harm after the decision; outcome coded HARM-CAPTURED or HARM-MISSED.

entries.problem: No independent verification capacity for frontier claims — Government and external parties cannot verify lab statements about capabilities or safeguards.

estate.note: Independent verification method: triple-blind roles, sealed predictions, blinded scoring, controls, permutation nulls.
Never assume capabilities from documentation alone; capability statuses require evidence.
Capability claims are a named attack surface.

adapter.finding: An unverified frontier claim becomes a claim object: the claim, the lab statement, the independent test it needs. (Overlaps A29; Source B restates it as a governance problem.)
adapter.patch: An independent verification run becomes the gated output; the claim's status moves only on the result.

entries.problem: Liability and accountability gaps for autonomous actions — Legal frameworks lag (e.g., bars on 'the AI did it' defenses in some jurisdictions, but enforcement is weak).

estate.note: Insured Action Protocol: Intent, Risk Scalar, micro-premium, Tactile Token, unlock, record in Append-Only History; the manufacturer is not the regulator.
Governance rules the loop cannot change without founder-approved governance change.

entries.gap: The insured-action protocol is a design; legal enforcement is outside the estate, and no jurisdiction's framework is wired into the loop.

indicators.name: Autonomous actions with an insured-action record

adapter.patch: An insured-action record (priced, permitted, recorded) becomes the gated output; the action does not move without it.
adapter.retest: Check the action against its record; outcome coded ACCOUNTABILITY-RECORDED or ACCOUNTABILITY-GAPPED.

entries.problem: Compositional security is missing — Security is treated as a property of individual models rather than of the permission and architecture composition (intelligence vs. authority separation).

The intersection gate is where separate judgments meet.

entries.problem: Harvest-now-decrypt-later (quantum) — Encrypted traffic and data captured today become valuable once cryptographically relevant quantum computers exist. Long-tail confidentiality risk that is hard to measure in real time.
entries.gap: The estate has no quantum-risk model, no crypto-agility plan, and no harvest-now tracking: no inventory of what is encrypted with quantum-vulnerable algorithms, and no measurement of the exposure.

adapter.retest: TO BUILD: re-measure the exposure after migration; outcome coded EXPOSURE-REDUCED or EXPOSURE-UNCHANGED.

entries.problem: Fragmented operational data in critical infrastructure — Systems that cannot assemble a coherent picture under stress (cyber, physical, market).

estate.note: Signal nervous system and event substrate; findings flow as events through the lattice with provenance.
Signal intake, scoring, ranking, action; the intake pattern for assembling a picture from fragmented sources.
Searchable registry of all 179 systems; the inventory is the picture's index.

entries.gap: The estate has an event substrate and a registry, but no stress-tested operational picture for critical infrastructure: coherence under stress has never been measured. Same gap as A78.

indicators.name: Mean time to a coherent picture

adapter.patch: A lattice integration (every source flows as an event with provenance) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Stress-test the picture; outcome coded PICTURE-COHERENT or PICTURE-FRAGMENTED.

entries.problem: Organizational silos as the dominant barrier — Technology exists; ownership, approval speed, and cross-team coordination do not.

estate.note: Elastic organization creation: temporary teams that dissolve; permanent infrastructure is NOT the default.
Seven legions under one registry and one mission loop; the organism model dissolves silos inside one system.
Event substrate: findings flow as events across the organism, not through siloed handoffs.

entries.gap: The organism model dissolves silos inside one system; it does not dissolve silos between organizations. Same gap as A95.

adapter.finding: A silo failure becomes a claim object: the decision, the teams that were not consulted, the defense that failed.
adapter.patch: A cross-team formation (smallest competent team across the silo) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Re-run the decision with cross-team input; outcome coded SILO-DISSOLVED or SILO-PERSISTS.

entries.problem: Incentive misalignment for secure-by-design and verification — Short-term cost and schedule dominate measurable long-term resilience.

estate.note: Micro-premium per action prices the risk now, so the short-term cost includes the long-term risk.
Value of information prices the decision; the long-term value is computed, not assumed.
Definition of done includes release evidence sealed and human acceptance recorded.

entries.gap: VOI and micro-premiums price security inside the estate's own builds, but long-term resilience is not yet priced as a number an external organization can act on. Same gap as A38/A92.

indicators.name: Decisions with a priced security premium

adapter.finding: An incentive misalignment becomes a claim object: the short-term cost, the long-term resilience at stake, the decision that chose cost.
adapter.patch: A priced decision packet (VOI plus micro-premium) becomes the gated output; the long-term cost is on the packet.
adapter.retest: Compare the actual cost after the decision; outcome coded RESILIENCE-PRICED or COST-ONLY.

entries.problem: Authority drift in long-running or multi-agent systems — Permissions expand or are reinterpreted without explicit re-authorization.

estate.note: Authority drift is a named attack surface; the court attacks the drift, not the agent.
Capability statuses and canary ladder; a permission change requires evidence.
Drift detector catches docs and permissions diverging from the proven version; canonical freeze locks it.

adapter.finding: An authority drift becomes a claim object: the permission, the drift, the re-authorization it lacked.
adapter.patch: A drift correction (recompile the authority mask, re-authorize explicitly) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Re-check the authority mask; outcome coded DRIFT-CORRECTED or DRIFT-PERSISTS.

entries.problem: No machine-readable canon with provenance, falsifiers, and lineage — Claims float without attached evidence or conditions under which they would be withdrawn.

estate.note: Master Codex v1.1.0: machine-readable canon; every claim with provenance, scope, confidence, falsifiers, and lineage.
Governance rules the loop cannot change without founder-approved governance change.
Machine-readable canon gate; the canon is the standard the loop is checked against.

adapter.finding: A floating claim becomes a claim object: the claim, the provenance it lacks, the falsifier it needs, the lineage it has no record of.
adapter.patch: A canon entry (provenance, falsifier, lineage) becomes the gated output; the claim does not enter the canon without it.
adapter.retest: Check the claim against the canon; outcome coded CLAIM-CANONICAL or CLAIM-FLOATING.

entries.problem: Swarm / multi-agent independence illusions — 20 identical agents are treated as 20 independent confirmations.

estate.note: Swarm diversity enforced; 20 identical agents are not 20 independent opinions; information gain per agent gates spawning.
Phase 1 isolation: seven agents record private judgments first; identical agents do not produce independent judgments.
Phantom-consensus measurement and dependence-aware pooling (scaled log-odds); composed confidence discounts correlation.

indicators.name: Consensus decisions with independent private records
Composed confidence vs majority confidence gap

adapter.finding: An independence illusion becomes a claim object: the consensus, the agents behind it, how many were actually independent.
adapter.patch: A diversity requirement (independent private records, dependence-aware pooling) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Re-run the consensus with diversity enforced; outcome coded CONSENSUS-INDEPENDENT or CONSENSUS-ILLUSION.

entries.problem: Economic models for sustained open-source security — Volume of findings grows; the capacity to validate, fix, and maintain does not.
entries.gap: The estate has no economic model for sustained open-source security: no funding model, no validation-capacity scaling, no maintainer resourcing. Same gap as A40 and B41.

adapter.finding: TO BUILD: an economic intake turning each open-source dependency into a claim object: finding volume, validation capacity, the gap.
adapter.patch: TO BUILD: an economic model (fund validation capacity to match finding volume) as the gated output.
adapter.retest: TO BUILD: re-measure capacity vs volume; outcome coded CAPACITY-MATCHES or CAPACITY-LAGS.

entries.problem: Real-time independent verification of agent actions at machine speed — Current gates are either too slow or too coarse.

estate.note: Dynamic verification intensity scales with risk, novelty, irreversibility, blast radius, and uncertainty; the intensity is the speed/accuracy trade-off.
Intersection gate enforced at runtime; the gate is per-action, not streaming.
Receipts at each stage; the chain is the verification record.

entries.gap: Gates exist but are not real-time at machine speed: verification is per-action and per-stage, not streaming; a fast agent can outrun the gate.

adapter.finding: A verification lag becomes a claim object: the action, the gate that was too slow, the actions that passed unverified.
adapter.patch: A streaming verification gate (intensity scaled by risk, fast path for low-risk actions) becomes the gated output.
adapter.retest: Measure verification latency after the change; outcome coded VERIFICATION-REAL-TIME or VERIFICATION-LAGGING.

entries.problem: Outcome coding that distinguishes 'action occurred' from 'action caused the result' — Causal attribution remains weak.

estate.note: Causal attribution: outcome after action does not prove the action caused it; the lab's core rule.
Episode records capture the action and the outcome separately, so the attribution can be checked.
Controls and permutation nulls: an outcome is caused only if it beats the null.

indicators.name: Outcomes coded as caused vs merely occurred

adapter.finding: An unattributed outcome becomes a claim object: the action, the outcome, the causal link it lacks.
adapter.patch: A causal attribution (control comparison, permutation null) becomes the gated output; the outcome is coded as caused only if it beats the null.
adapter.retest: Re-run the attribution against controls; outcome coded CAUSED or MERELY-OCCURRED.
